_comment: Coverage matrix for the shared Carve spec corpus (spec/tests/corpus/*.crv). Every NN-slug base category must appear in covered or skip; the coverage-matrix test fails otherwise so a new spec category forces a classify decision. covered = grammar parses every file in the category with no ERROR/MISSING node. skip = at least one file currently produces an ERROR/MISSING node; reason records the unmodeled construct (a grammar gap to surface, not to hack around). A skip key is a CATEGORY (NN-slug) or a single EXAMPLE (NN-slug-2) — use the example form when the rest of the category parses cleanly, so one gap does not drop assertion for its siblings. A key equal to a category name is read as the CATEGORY, so the first example of a category cannot be skipped on its own. REASONS: a ledger entry's `reason` may be `ref:<key>`, resolving against the top-level `reasons` map, so one grammar gap spanning a whole category states its explanation once. coverage-matrix gates it both ways - a ref with no entry fails, and a reasons entry nothing references fails, because a reason nobody points at is an excuse that outlived the gap it excused.

reasons.reference-definition-absorbed: a reference definition the language collects - the fixture shows none of its text - is paragraph text in the tree. Two causes, both in `src/scanner.c` (tree-sitter-carve#372): `close_paragraph` has no probe that lets a `[label]:` definition interrupt an open paragraph, only the footnote form; and a continued definition list keeps its first item's content column, so a description padded differently from its term is measured against the term's column and the definition opener refuses it.
reasons.a-column-0-opener-does-not-close-an-open: a column-0 block opener does not close an open LIST; it folds into the item as lazy paragraph text. `- a` / `# H` builds no heading, while `> q` / `# H` does - so the block quote closes correctly and only the list does not. Both documents here reach it through a `+` continuation marker, which this grammar opens as an ordinary bullet list, after which the column-0 heading below is swallowed the same way.
reasons.a-tabbed-frontmatter-opener-swallows-the: `---` followed by a TAB is not a frontmatter opener, and the grammar agrees that far - it builds no frontmatter. But it then reads the closing `---` three lines down as an `em_dash` inside the still-open paragraph rather than as a thematic break, so the `<hr>` the fixture expects between the paragraph and `body` is not built.
reasons.an-attribute-line-does-not-end-the-parag: a floating attribute line at column 0 does not end the paragraph above it, so the list it is meant to attach to never opens: `para` / `{.x}` / `- b` is ONE paragraph. The fixture expects the paragraph to end at the attribute line and the run to reach the list below it, as `<ul class="x">`.
reasons.fence-on-a-marker-line-builds-nothing: a code fence opened on a list MARKER line: the item closes with an EMPTY code block and the residue re-parses at document level when the body sits BELOW the item's content column (markup-carve/carve#646). This grammar builds no code_block for any of these, and MEASURED against it, the cause is NOT that the fence is committed to the item with no route out - it is that the fence never opens at all. `parse_backtick` refuses an opener when `has_extra_indent` is true, and on a marker line the fence sits past the line's own indent while the item's content column is only established by the marker itself, so `- ` + fence is read as inline verbatim. The heading marker and the colon fence carry the same column-0 guard and fail the same way on a marker line, while a block quote and a table - which do not - open there correctly. The quote half of that was narrower than it reads and is now closed: its MARKER opened, but the quote took no content and the rest of the line was ejected from the list, repaired in tree-sitter-carve#218 by moving the line's content margin to the quote's own content column when it opens on an item's marker line - the same move this entry's openers need at the LIST marker. So the first half is a column question and the second half, closing the item at the boundary, is the container change; the fully-indented example (-3) needs only the first. Tracked in tree-sitter-carve#160.
reasons.marker-line-block-opener-builds-nothing: a block opener written on a list MARKER line builds nothing. `- # H` gives a list item whose content is a PARAGRAPH, not a heading; `- ---` is read as a document-level thematic break that consumes the marker, so no list is built at all. Verified against the indented spelling, which works: `- a` / `  # H` does build the heading. This is the same shape as the recorded `fence-on-a-marker-line-builds-nothing` - the marker line is one position this grammar does not run block-opener recognition in - now reached by the heading and thematic-break openers too. A TASK checkbox does not change which openers reach it, but it does change what the thematic break degrades INTO, and the sentence above is wrong for that spelling: `- [x] # h` is still a paragraph, while `- [ ] ---` no longer consumes the marker - the list and the item ARE built and `---` becomes an inline `em_dash` inside the item's paragraph. Measured against the neighbour that works, which is what keeps the checkbox out of it: `- [ ] > q` opens its quote with content, so the checkbox does not disturb an opener the marker line already admits. That is why a-task-item-s-checkbox-is-not-decided-by-its-first-block reports `heading: want 1 have 0; thematic_break: want 1 have 0` and no gap for its quote.

skip.a-continuation-marker-attaches-one-block: a `+` continuation marker that attaches NOTHING - the line after it opens a sibling item rather than a block to attach - leaves the first item unclosed and the whole document parses to one top-level ERROR. `- a` / `+` / `- x` / `- y` is three flat items in the fixture. The category's other eight examples, where the marker does attach a block, parse cleanly.
skip.a-quoted-attribute-value-stops-at-the-ne: a quoted attribute value carrying a newline (`{k="a` / `b"}`) parses to ERROR. The corpus pins it as literal text - the inline block does not span lines - but this grammar commits to an attribute block on the opening brace and has no route back to a paragraph when the value never closes on its line. Same class as an-attribute-name-admits-no-colon-3. The category's other examples parse cleanly.

an-all-blank-raw-payload-still-emits-its.reason: the source deliberately opens a raw block whose payload is one blank line. Its expected HTML is therefore only a newline, which has no HTML element for the comparison pass to count; the raw_block node is the correct source structure rather than a grammar error.

a-caret-line-does-not-end-a-paragraph-it.reason: a caret line after ordinary prose is paragraph text, but the context-free grammar cannot make caption recognition depend on whether the preceding block is one of the five captionable hosts, so it builds a caption node here. The renderer/parser implementations apply the host check and keep the line literal.

an-unresolved-image-gives-its-whole-capt.reason: the same host check as a-caret-line-does-not-end-a-paragraph-it-cannot-caption, reached by the one host whose captionability is not decidable from the line at all. `![a][r]` / `^ cap one` is a captionable IMAGE only if `[r]` resolves, and whether it resolves is a fact about the whole document. Measured against this category's own -2, which is byte-identical for the first three lines and adds `[r]: /u` five lines down: the grammar builds the same caption node in both, so the caption here is not a defect in the caret rule but the reference resolution a context-free grammar has no access to. The renderer resolves the reference first and keeps this line literal, which is why the expected HTML is one paragraph.

a-caret-line-does-not-end-a-paragraph-it.reason: a paragraph that merely contains an image is not a captionable host; deciding that the image is the paragraph's whole content needs semantic context beyond this grammar's local caret-line rule, so it over-accepts the caret line as a caption.

an-unresolved-reference-image-takes-no-c.reason: `![a][nope]` + `^ cap` is one paragraph: the reference does not resolve, so the image is literal text and the `^` line is literal with it. Whether it resolves depends on the DEFINITIONS in the document, which a context-free grammar does not have - so the caption is built here and cannot be declined without a symbol table. The renderer decides correctly; highlighting a caption that the language declines is the cost.

generic-divs-4.reason: the current engine accepts a numeric custom admonition kind in `::: 123`, while the grammar's admonition identifier begins with a letter and leaves the fence as paragraph text. The grammar and its named `admonition_type` token need a deliberate identifier-policy update rather than silently widening during a corpus bump.

an-empty-unterminated-container-ends-at-.reason: an admonition opened on a description marker line is treated as definition text; the marker-line block-opener path does not open the container.

a-block-opener-past-a-nested-footnote-de.reason: after collecting a footnote definition inside a list item, the scanner leaves the following heading inside the footnote paragraph instead of returning to the item at its authored column.

list-nesting-and-looseness-9.reason: extra marker padding before a task checkbox sets a wider item content column than the scanner records, so the heading aligned to that column folds into paragraph text.

a-continuation-row-s-open-run-and-an-esc.reason: an ESCAPED closing pipe leaves the row unterminated: `| a b \|` is a paragraph where the fixture expects a table whose one cell holds `a b |`. The row closes on that pipe because the line ends in one, and the escape decides only what the CELL holds - but `scan_table_cell` reads `\|` as one escape pair and advances over both characters, so the pipe that terminates the row is eaten before the terminator check can see it. Nothing to do with an unclosed run: this document holds no verbatim run at all, which is why it no longer shares a reason with the rest of its category.

a-frontmatter-opener-takes-exactly-one-s.reason: `---<SP><SP>yaml` is no longer read as a frontmatter opener - the opener's `[space]` slot takes exactly one space and the line is prose - but the `---` three lines below it, which the language turns into a thematic break, is folded into that prose instead. A thematic break does not interrupt an open paragraph in this grammar; `paragraph-interruption-3` records the same gap on a document with no frontmatter in it, and the two close together.

a-quoted-attribute-value-stops-at-the-ne.reason: the cr spelling parses to a different tree because the LF spelling already parses to ERROR - the quoted attribute value carrying a newline is the skip recorded for this example. It arrived as one of three example-level skips on the same corpus bump; the other two - a line holding only a vertical tab, form feed, NEL, LS or PS, and a content line ending in NBSP, ZWSP, BOM or U+2000 - were both control characters with no line-content route, and both are closed. This one is not a character the text token can admit: the attribute block commits on the opening brace and has no route back to a paragraph when the value never closes on its line. The terminator is not the defect here, the unmodeled construct is, and the divergence goes away with it. Tracked in tree-sitter-carve#160.
